citeAs: Badertdinov, I., Golubev, A., Nekrashevich, M., Shevtsov, A., Karasik, S., Andriushchenko, A., Trofimova, M., Litvintseva, D., Yangel, B. (2025). SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents. NeurIPS 2025 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks.
creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel (Nebius)
description: SWE-rebench is a public dataset of over 21,000 interactive Python-based software engineering tasks extracted from real-world GitHub repositories via a fully automated pipeline. Each task instance is grounded in a real GitHub issue and pull request, includes executable environments, solution patches, test patches, and LLM-assessed quality annotations, making it suitable for reinforcement learning of SWE agents at scale and for contamination-free benchmarking.
name: SWE-rebench
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The fine-tuned Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model was evaluated against the vanilla Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct baseline on 413 validation examples. For Task Complexity: fine-tuned achieved 81% accuracy and weighted F1 of 0.82 (vs. 68% accuracy for baseline). For Test Patch Correctness: 67% accuracy (weighted F1: 0.65). For Issue Clarity: 79% accuracy (weighted F1: 0.76). Detailed per-class precision and recall are reported in Table 4 of the paper.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Automated quality assessment using a fine-tuned Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model trained on human annotations from SWE-bench Verified. For each task instance, the model receives the issue description, canonical solution patch, and test patch, and independently predicts three binary quality labels: Issue Clarity (whether the issue description is sufficiently detailed), Task Complexity (estimated effort to resolve), and Test Patch Correctness (whether tests accurately verify the fix). A 75/25 training/validation split was used on over 3,800 SWE-bench Verified examples (413 validation examples).
rai:dataBiases: 1. The dataset is limited to Python repositories, introducing a language bias. 2. Only repositories with permissive licenses are included, which may skew toward certain types of open-source projects. 3. Only repositories where Python constitutes over 75% of codebase LOC are included. 4. The automated quality assessment model was trained on SWE-bench Verified annotations, which may introduce biases from that dataset's manual curation process. 5. The benchmark subset is restricted to issues created in 2025 and written in English, limiting temporal and linguistic diversity.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected via an automated four-stage pipeline: (1) Preliminary task collection from GitHub Archive and GitHub repositories — approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025, from over 30,000 repositories with permissive licenses where Python constitutes over 75% of codebase lines; (2) Automated installation instruction configuration using an LLM (Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct) to generate environment setup recipes; (3) Execution-based installation verification in isolated containers; (4) Automated instance quality assessment using a fine-tuned LLM. The pipeline yielded 21,336 valid, annotated task instances from 3,468 distinct GitHub repositories.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Approximately 95% of task instances receive a version via git tag; the remaining ~5% are assigned a unique version so each uses its own environment. Tasks with flaky tests (due to external API calls or floating-point precision issues) are excluded by running tests multiple times. Tasks where installation fails (e.g., unpinned/obsolete dependencies, lack of interactivity during installation) are excluded — the overall acceptance rate from ~150K filtered tasks to ~21K valid tasks is approximately 14%.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sourced from GitHub Archive (daily JSON archives of public GitHub events including issue descriptions, discussions, linked pull requests, and metadata) and directly cloned GitHub repositories with full commit histories. Approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues from over 30,000 repositories were downloaded as the initial raw input.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025 were collected. The benchmark subset uses issues created in 2025 (January and March–April 2025 subsets are specifically analyzed).
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Software Collection
rai:dataLimitations: 1. Automated task quality assessment may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue, leading to lower absolute success rates compared to manually curated benchmarks. 2. The initial release is limited exclusively to Python, restricting applicability to other language ecosystems. 3. The agentless LLM-based installation approach was validated on only 18 repositories for prompt engineering and may not capture every project's subtleties. 4. The automated pipeline relies on heuristics and LLM-driven interpretations that may not fully replicate nuanced human judgment.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Task instances are grouped by project version (normalized to major.minor format from git tags) and share a single environment per version group. For each version group, the base_commit of the most recent pull request is selected. Patches are generated by diffing head_commit against base_commit (falling back to merge_commit if head_commit is unavailable) to isolate branch-specific changes. Deleted test files are filtered out from test directives. Tasks with flaky tests (external API calls or floating-point precision issues) are excluded by running tests multiple times and excluding instances that fail in at least one run.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Multi-stage filtering applied to raw pull requests: (1) Repository must be Python (>75% LOC) with a permissive license; (2) Issue must be marked as resolved; (3) PR must be merged into main branch; (4) PR must not be linked to multiple issues; (5) Issue description must be longer than 10 characters; (6) PR must introduce or modify tests and include code changes beyond test files; (7) Changes must affect 1 to 15 files. Each PR's overall patch is split into a solution patch (non-test files) and a test patch (test files only). Repository versions are normalized to major.minor format using git tags. Dependency versions are frozen via pip freeze and conda env export after successful environment setup.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The pipeline is designed for continuous collection of fresh tasks. The SWE-rebench leaderboard is continuously updated with new tasks and model evaluations. Future work includes expanding data coverage to non-issue-linked PRs, improving task filtering, supporting new programming languages (JavaScript, Java, C++), and maintaining evaluation on fresh tasks for existing and new models.
rai:dataSocialImpact: SWE-rebench may accelerate the development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering, which brings potential risks such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities. The authors believe that fostering openness, decontaminated evaluations, and rigorous benchmarking practices helps mitigate these concerns and contributes to responsible advancement of the field.
rai:dataUseCases: 1. Training LLM-based software engineering agents, particularly via reinforcement learning (RL) approaches that require interactive tasks with automatic verification. 2. Evaluating LLM-based agents on real-world software engineering tasks in a contamination-free setting via the SWE-rebench leaderboard. 3. Benchmarking and comparing open- and closed-source models on standardized SWE tasks. 4. Studying data contamination effects in existing benchmarks like SWE-bench Verified.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (used for generating environment installation recipes — identifying relevant files, extracting installation recipes, and iterative recipe refinement); a fine-tuned Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model (used for automated quality assessment of Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness, fine-tuned on SWE-bench Verified human annotations).

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper does not specify a fixed number of independent annotations per item; quality labels are predicted by a single fine-tuned model per label type.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotation is automated (machine-generated via fine-tuned LLM); no human annotator demographics are described for the SWE-rebench dataset itself (SWE-bench Verified human annotations used for training are not described demographically).
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Annotation is fully automated using fine-tuned LLM models; no external annotation platform (e.g., MTurk) is used.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values is described; missing data is handled by exclusion rather than imputation.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of GitHub issues, pull requests, and code from public repositories; no personal or sensitive information collection is described.
